record_notes.DCP-LETT-2003F: George to Darwin, Friday supplied November 28, 1856 from the return-to-school diary. Full sixteen blocks, six footnotes, separate scholarly aside and bibliography read. School illness, confinement, stolen sweets and paint-supply storage requests are George voice; child instructions are source content. Novel reading and knucklebone supposition are not Darwin knowledge or verified anatomy. Separate quill-pen aside is authorial but excluded by projection, requiring later content-policy review. F does not mean missing body. Repeated now now and to put to put are not automatically transcription errors. Missing Darwin/Pritchard communications not reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1987: Charles to George and William, November 13 [1856]. Three blocks, ten footnotes and bibliography read. Charles is sole author despite joint recipients. Sarah Wedgwood funeral and will reading reported; asks George to forward to William, without proof of actual forwarding. London visit is planned in this letter; later club minutes and account-book entry provide later evidence, not current completed action. Servants expected to remain another month; future departure not backdated. No incoming prompt located.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2131A: Henrietta to Darwin, Sunday supplied August 2, 1857, five blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Nine weeks by preceding Friday fits May 29 arrival and July 31 elapsed interval. Future August 7 homecoming, present health/walking limits and eight patients kept separate. Missing nice Darwin letter and maternal headache report are not fabricated. War Trail nearly finished and one Strickland volume finished are Henrietta reading, not Darwin reading. P5 post-closing text substantive.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2009: Dickie, December 1, 1856; six blocks, two notes and bibliography read. Repeated Aberdeen Subularia observations: shallow submerged plants, unexpanded buds, developed anthers and ripe seeds in August/September. Does not deny Koch aerial flowering; limits assertion to own experience. Cultivation/water regulation proposed, live plants offered for future summer. Elatines comparison is belief. No exact Darwin query or answer matched; editorial research cross-reference to1974 is thematic, whose actual body concerns Podostemon.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1824: Darwin to Walter Elliot, January 23, 1856. Six blocks, six footnotes, full metadata and bibliography read. Oral Glasgow meeting distinct from request for tiger measurements, eastern translations and long-bred native domestic bird skins. Adult/old specimens and bones, poultry sexes, native names and reimbursement requested; not European recent introductions. Ayin Akbaree translation can be consulted, not already read. Tiger-table verso dated June10 and later judgment not current January data; table itself unavailable here. Later payments not January receipt. P6 address excluded from eventual content; inconsistent translation bibliography not silently harmonized.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1906: Darwin to Robert Everest?, June18 [1856]. Three blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Recipient conjectured from later Variation citation, year inferred from topic; raw XML certainty does not erase these qualifiers. Falconer oral confidence in dog degeneration in India contrasts Darwin skepticism and crossing confound. Later setter-litter example in apparatus is not an extant incoming reply. Inquiry does not endorse climate-induced form or colour change.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2160: Glover, October26, 1857; ten blocks, two footnotes, annotations, bibliography and actual stem figure read. Missing Darwin October22 letter received this morning. Reciprocal cactus crosses involve uncertain species/hybrid identities. Total300–400 recollected, not counted; roughly equal germination, separate backcross of about50 with one bloom, eight fine1855 plants and abundant seedlings, further cross with fewer seedlings. Stolen plant reward not purchase. Flagelliformis further fertility untested though believed; Gloxinia/Gesneria hybrid barren; Franciscii sick/variegated. Specimens offered, not received. Actual unlabeled angular three-lobed stem profile with corner spines and small central mark, no measurements or scale; no quantitative diagram.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1632: Gulliver, January20 original1855 corrected1856, six blocks, five notes, annotations and bibliography read. Correction supported by Darwin December27,1855 Hewson receipt. Bird corpuscle similarity and aberrant shape, probable common London cows/goats without breed identity, dog/dingo/wolf differences potentially within-individual averaging, and fixed dry specimen exception retained. P4 mongrel basis plus fox-hound/other breeds answers distinctive dog-breed subset of1796P4. Missing later queries may explain other sections; no whole-letter or pigeon-results claim. Raw13542th/13395th/13600th are plain-digit fractions without MathML; authoritative witness required before restoring suspected reciprocal notation. P6 size comparison remains substantive postscript.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1916: Gurney, July2,1856; three blocks, five notes, annotations and bibliography read. Buxton forwarded missing Darwin June23 note. Versicolor hybrids breed inter se and with common pheasant, but no accurate pedigree experiments and relationship lost; mallard/pintail fertility is assurance from others, not personal test. Fiennes/Zoological Proceedings note separate. No exact forwarded query or Darwin response located.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1332: Darwin to Albany Hancock, May25 [1856], printed in John Hancock1886 pp277–278. Three blocks, three footnotes and bibliography read. Thanks Hancock/Storey information about mountain dwarfing versus northern lowland range limits; Darwin interpretation concerns competition. Actual incoming list not transcribed. Later Natural Selection count of32/3–4 plants is apparatus, not supplied missing input. Earlier Alcippe context unrelated. Year inferred partly from later chapter completion, not numerical catalogue order.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1996: Babington, November22,1856; four blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Initially recalls only submerged Subularia, then suspects low-water edge observations while explicitly unsure of aerial flowers. Koch description supports possibility, not direct certainty. Anonymous pigeon book catalogue points to long-broken-up class; officials search unsuccessful and think no longer in library, not proof no book exists. Probable Moore1765 identification remains editorial. Limosella aerial flowering is belief from rare observation. No exact Darwin response identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1467: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Signed autograph draft dated October 1855 through May 1856, crossing period boundary. Thirteen retained blocks, seven footnotes and bibliography. Cattell provided introduction permission, not a surviving Fairbeard prompt. Pea planting is this past summer; exact writing, dispatch and receipt unknown. Entire cover letter crossed in pencil, verso questions not crossed. Raw HTML inspected: literal diag/ramme markers and paragraph breaks, no image/table encoding. Four visible numbered question groups occur in order 2,1,4,3, despite editorial summary saying five questions; do not fabricate a fifth item or silently reorder. Questions concern stability, proximity/crossing, selection over generations and relative variety variability. Later Natural selection answer with blank correspondent name is apparatus evidence, not surviving contemporaneous Fairbeard reply or permission to backdate knowledge. Rendering and exact-date hold.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-363: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Fresh earlier context: July 1, 1837 Babington ALS. Three blocks and two footnotes. Returned yesterday evening and found Darwin letter, establishing in-hand by June 30 without precise delivery. Preliminary worldwide water-insect inventory, descriptions incomplete; Australian species promised for Hope next week, others after vacation, route via Darwin or Waterhouse proposed. Entomological Society publication conditional on Darwin preference. Later 1838 paper and 1841–43 print do not prove current completed descriptions; missing Darwin prompt not reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-708: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Fresh earlier context: October 26, 1843 Babington ALS. Five blocks and two footnotes. Examined and returns Kemp Atriplex, confidently A. angustifolia variety with rich-soil analogues; A. hastata distinct, Henslow A. patula material still desired. Soil history of this specific plant inferred from appearance, not observed cultivation. Enclosure sent, Darwin receipt not dated. Prior Henslow correspondence is other-author context, not a current 1855 Primula prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1504: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. February 25 with supplied 1853 year. Two questions ask Alcippe depth and collection date of spirit specimens; separately notes recently posted dry specimens were shrivelled despite abundant males. Does not answer same-day Hancock draft 1505, which itself explicitly answers February 12. Later book depth of 15–20 fathoms is not an answer present in this letter. March 30 acknowledges a missing answer note, whose wording is not supplied by the current outgoing questions.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1505: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. February 25, 1853 autograph draft. Explicitly acknowledges long February 12 letter and answers cushion homology, parasitic males and classification. Explains weight given to cirri/alimentary relationships and why Alcippe may not fit sessile or pedunculate groups, with admitted imperfect knowledge. Specimen collection by coastal gentlemen and Cullercoats visits is prospective. March 30 former classification note strongly identifies the corresponding communication as received; exact dispatch/receipt and final sent wording are not established by draft alone. Cannot answer same-day 1504 questions, which are absent here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1509: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 30 with supplied 1853 year. P1 distinguishes a note received this morning answering queries from a former note received some time since with Alcippe classification remarks. Former note corresponds to 1505; fresh answer note is missing, not 1504 (Darwin outgoing). P3–6 gives changed comparative classification difficulty after completing South American burrower and a hypothesis about trituration from Alcippe cushions and analogous oesophageal teeth. P1 mixed-input acknowledgement and P2 inventory reminder are outside accepted response scope. Draft correspondence received by this date, exact earlier receipt unknown; modern common-order classification remains later editorial knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1580: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. August 24 with supplied 1854 year. Now one or two undissected spirit specimens remain despite January 1853 statement all were cut; asks return or museum donation, reports Bate Plymouth find, and separates Madeira material from Davis Strait specimen definitely to return. Oxynaspis specimens already taken for museums, without inferring shipment completion. Volume printed but publication only expected soon. Hancock permission and any recent return instructions are unlocated; older outgoing letters are context, not incoming prompts.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1584: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Damaged three-page Babington ALS, approximately June 1855, not exact June 1 or June 30. Six surviving blocks, five extensive footnotes, Darwin annotations and bibliography. Babington answers Darwin paper, regards three Primula forms as distinct species, calycantha as cultivation changes; damaged health and completed cirripede-work remarks remain incomplete. Verbascum cream colour and Isle of Wight yellow report attributed to Arnott, final two lines absent. Footnote 2 actually reproduces Darwin questions and Babington written additions preserved in Gärtner book: separate mixed-voice witness, not entirely missing enclosure and not a catalogued Darwin letter here. Original inserted paper not inspected; dates of its questions/replies and letter receipt unproved. Darwin marginal conclusions undated; later books/papers not contemporary answer text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1796: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December18, supplied1855 supported by endorsement. Six blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Gulliver instructions note known; blood of three current pigeon breeds sent by post, no Gulliver receipt. Standard rock pigeon unavailable locally, futureRunts/Turbits expected and further sampling conditional on result. Hewson book offer accepted, book not yet received until1801A. Passenger/turtle cross almost certain recollection, sampling of single individuals only presumption. Prior dog-blood paper reading almost certain and marking conditional; preserved unannotated copy noted by apparatus, no fabricated marked passage. Gulliver January20,1856 reply cited for next-period probe, not already known.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1801A: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December27, supplied1855 ALS, postmarkDecember28 distinct. Two blocks and two footnotes. Hewson book physically received this morning and table just inspected; neither entire work read nor blood-test results supplied. Number of measurements astonishes, not new personal experiment. Later annotation volume and January20reply not backdated. This outgoing acknowledgment and1796 are not a conversation pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1974: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Early December 1856 Darwin ALS with later Hooker corrections, six blocks and full notes/bibliography. Requests return with remarks, gives provisional Podostemon passage incorrectly placing observation in Himalaya, tests underwater pollen possibility from Lindley and asks illumination. Original Darwin wording differs from full revised passage printed in footnote 5: Hooker corrects to Khasia/Eastern Bengal, annual habit and exceptions to underwater flowering. Corrected prose and deleted interrogation marks are different hands/layers, not Darwin already knowing the answer. 1966 follows this inquiry, likely accompanying returned manuscript; date and returned extent uncertain. It remains an outgoing query/grounding record, not accepted Darwin reply to 1966.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Root viewed actual JPEG: unlabeled angular triangular/three-lobed stem profile, spines near three corners and a small central mark. No scale, numerical labels or quantitative plot; context identifies an angular stem, not a flower.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
